title: A hospital ward: the bed off the wall with its kit round it, a washroom to each ward
rule: A ward is a room about 232 by 304 under 128 for one bed (two at most), with its own washroom 152 by 112 under 120. The bed is a loose prop standing 32 to 56 off the wall (never against it), often turned 3 to 20; round it an IV stand 42 to 51 away, a cart 52 to 58, a bedside cabinet 16 off the wall with a monitor on it, a radiator on the wall, a wall rail at 36, and over the bed's head a tube on the wall at 64 up, tilted 75, lighting the pillow. The washroom holds a bath 16 off the wall, a basin and a toilet, a radiator and a rail by the bath. Our clinic is the owner's field hospital (four beds in one ward with screens): ask the owner first before changing it; use this for a new hospital or clinic piece.

Within 128 of the ward beds: hospital_ivstand01 42 to 51, hospital_cart01 52 to 58, hospital_shelf01 53 to 87 (16 off its wall, 18 up), consolebox03a 57 to 111 (36 up, on the shelf), radiator01a 111 to 124 (21 up, on the wall), lights_florescent01a at 64 up pitched 75 (9 of 34) with a light_spot 220 235 245 600 cone 40 pitch -35 and a point 20. Nine washrooms all 152 by 112 by 120: bathtub01a 16 off, furnituresink001a 8 to 16 off at 23 up, furnituretoilet001a 16 off, a radiator, hospital_railing pieces. Ours (map_mods_b.py m_clinic): a ward 576 by 320 under 160 with four beds along its back wall and cloth screens between.

Sizes come from the models (map_assets.py).

title: An operating theatre: the table in the middle, two lamps held still and turned, scrub sinks
rule: The operating table is fixed and square, 48 to 120 from every wall, in a room 288 to 451 wide under 124 to 192 (a big theatre has three tables in a row 92 apart). Over each table hang one to three surgery lamps about 100 over the floor and 24 to 32 under the ceiling, each rolled 45 and turned its own way so they cross over the table; they are physics props held still (no damage, motion off). Beside: a pair of scrub sinks on a wall, monitors on a cart or shelf, an IV stand, a cart. Our clinic's theatre lamp hangs from its top and shines straight down: ask the owner first before changing it.

title: A hospital corridor: 224 wide, a rail all along both walls, benches with a picture over each

title: A building without power: lamps named and off until the power comes back, flares and signs in the dark
rule: To make a place dark that can be lit again, its lamps are real lights named in banks and set to start off, each a warm cage lamp spot (254 216 146 75, cone 70, pitch -70) with a glow sprite 10 under it, turned on together when the power is restored. In the dark, a road flare on the floor carries an orange light (254 174 10, 100 to 200) 12 over it, a green sprite marks the exit, a blue light by sparking wires. Even dark places keep a light within about 200 to 350 of most of their floor. In Living City this suits an outage or a raid's cut power: ask the owner first, since it is a new feature (and never a flicker style).

title: A car park: 112 clear, columns every 256, two cars to a bay, a deck that slopes 1 in 12

The deck itself slopes about 4.8 degrees (1 in 12), or decks are joined by ramps of 9.2 degrees (1 in 6) 224 to 240 wide. Bay lines, arrows and letters are overlays on the floor; wall markings on the columns. Cars mostly nose in (yaw square to the wall, 2 in 3), a few turned free; the kit is fluorescent tubes, sprinklers, pipes along the ceiling, power boxes, cones, a dumpster, bicycles, handrails along the ramps. A new piece, if the owner wants one. Pieces already built keep their look: ask the owner first before changing them.

title: A fallen floor: the slab broken into tilted pieces, what stood on it slid down with it
